title: Why do we get goosebumps?
examples: Teacher, why do I get goosebumps when it gets cold?
What are those little bumps on my skin?
Does getting goosebumps mean I am cold?

explain.say: When you feel cold, your skin can get goosebumps.

items: Body tries to keep you warm

explain.say: Tiny muscles in your skin pull your hairs up.

draw.text: Muscles pull hairs up when cold

explain.say: Furry animals look bigger when their fur stands up.
In furry animals, raised fur traps warm air. People have little hair, so it helps us only a little.
You might see goosebumps after a swim in cold water.
Sometimes you get them without being cold. A big feeling, like excitement, can cause them.

items: Seeing something surprising can trigger it

faq.q: Why do I get goosebumps when I am scared?
faq.a: When you feel scared, your body gets ready for action. Goosebumps are part of that.
asks: Is it always about being cold?

faq.q: Do I still get goosebumps if I have very short hair?
faq.a: Yes. The tiny muscles still pull, even when the hairs are short.
asks: Can I still get them without hair?

faq.q: Are goosebumps a sign that I am sick?
faq.a: No, they are just a normal way your body tries to keep you warm. They do not mean you are getting sick.

faq.q: What are those tiny muscles called?
faq.a: These muscles are called arrector pili muscles. They are very small muscles attached to your hair roots.

faq.q: Is this happening in all animals?
faq.a: Yes. Many furry animals and birds fluff up to keep warm.
asks: Is this natural for all creatures?

facts: Goosebumps happen because tiny muscles pull hairs up.
This action helps trap a layer of warm air near the skin.
The body uses this trick to help keep you warm.
It can happen when you are cold, or when you feel excited.

quiz.say: Tiny muscles in your skin pull something up. What do they pull?
quiz.show: 🥶 What do the tiny muscles pull up?
quiz.why: Each tiny muscle is joined to a hair. It pulls the hair up.

wrong.0: Bones are deep inside, and these muscles are in the skin.
wrong.2: Nails grow at the ends of your fingers and toes.

quiz.say: A furry cat fluffs up its fur on a cold day. How does that help?
quiz.why: Fluffed-up fur traps a layer of warm air next to the skin.

wrong.1: Fluffing up keeps the cat warm, and it is no itch.
wrong.2: Fur stays dry, and fluffing up traps air.

options.show: when you are cold or excited
options.say: when you are cold or excited

quiz.why: Cold and big feelings, like excitement, can both cause goosebumps.

wrong.0: Goosebumps come with cold or big feelings.
wrong.1: Eating is a different thing, and goosebumps come with cold.
